plan: In a single-round auction with values drawn from $0-$49, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. With a $31 value, I want to win without overpaying. Other rational bidders likely have similar incentives. I'll bid strategically around $25-$28 - high enough to likely win, but leaving room to profit if my value is near the median range. This allows potential profit while avoiding overbidding.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with values between $0-$49, the optimal strategy is typically to bid close to, but slightly below, my true value. With a $37 value, rational opponents will likely bid near their own values. I want to win if my value is higher, but avoid overpaying. A bid around $36-$36.5 seems strategic - high enough to likely win if I have a top value, but not risking overpaying by bidding my full $37.

In a second-price sealed bid auction with values between $0-$49, the optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. My value is $11. Other bidders are also rational. They likely won't bid much above their own values. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances, but not so high that I risk negative earnings. A bid around $15 seems strategic - high enough to potentially win, but not overcommitting.
